classification.difficultyReason: Model constant reading rates, scale the original durations from 200 to 300 pages, compare the resulting times, and convert a fractional minute into seconds.

content.prompt: Sarah takes 4 hours and 45 minutes to read a 200-page novel, while Derek takes 5 hours and 2 minutes. Now they both read a 300-page novel. If they read at the same speeds as for the previous novel, how much faster than Derek will Sarah finish the 300-page novel?

answer.short:
25 minutes 30 seconds earlier (1530 seconds).

Use each reader’s time per page to find their time for 300 pages, then compare.
answer.worked:
Convert the original reading times to minutes:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Sarah's time for 200 pages}&=4\times60+45=285\text{ min}\\\text{Derek's time for 200 pages}&=5\times60+2=302\text{ min}\end{align*}$$

Find the time for one page, then multiply by 300:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Sarah's time for 1 page}&=\frac{285}{200}\text{ min}\\\text{Sarah's time for 300 pages}&=\frac{285}{200}\times300=427.5\text{ min}\\\text{Derek's time for 1 page}&=\frac{302}{200}\text{ min}\\\text{Derek's time for 300 pages}&=\frac{302}{200}\times300=453\text{ min}\\\text{Time difference}&=453-427.5=25.5\text{ min}\\\text{Time difference}&=25\text{ min }30\text{ s}=1530\text{ s}\end{align*}$$

Sarah finishes 25 minutes 30 seconds earlier.
